summary: Defines an IPv6 Address Specific BGP Extended Community attribute. RFC 4360 had only an IPv4 version, which is a problem for applications that need to tag routes with an IPv6 address. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: BGP routes can carry small tags that mark them with an address. There was a tag for the old kind of address only. This document adds one for the newer, longer kind.

subtitle: A BGP extended community that carries a 16-octet IPv6 address, for networks that cannot rely on IPv4 addresses.

tldr.problem: BGP Extended Communities (RFC 4360) have an IPv4 Address Specific form but no IPv6 one, which is a problem when an application built on the IPv4 form must run in a pure IPv6 environment.
tldr.mechanism: Because every Extended Community is 8 octets long, an IPv6 address cannot fit, so RFC 5701 defines a new optional transitive BGP attribute whose entries are 20 octets: a type, a sub-type, a 16-octet IPv6 Global Administrator and a 2-octet Local Administrator.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that assigns attribute value 25 and two community types, Route Target and Route Origin. The index lists it as updated by RFC 7153 and RFC 7606.

today: RFC 5701 is a Proposed Standard, and the index lists it as updated by RFC 7153 and RFC 7606. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why a New Attribute Is Needed
sections.content:
BGP Extended Communities, defined in RFC 4360, include an IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community but no IPv6 counterpart. An application that uses the IPv4 form therefore has a problem in a pure IPv6 environment.

The obstacle is size. The Extended Community attribute defines each community as 8 octets long, so a 16-octet IPv6 address cannot be added to it. RFC 5701 instead defines a separate BGP attribute with a structure similar to the IPv4 form, usable as a replacement for it.
sections.eli5: The old name tag is a small sticker with room for a short address only. A long address will not fit, so a bigger sticker is needed.

sections.title: The IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community
sections.content:
The attribute is a transitive, optional BGP attribute made up of a set of IPv6 Address Specific extended communities. Every route carrying it belongs to the communities listed. Each community is encoded in 20 octets.

  • The first octet is 0x00 if the sub-type is transitive across Autonomous Systems and 0x40 if not.
  • The second octet is the sub-type. The sub-types are the same as for the IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community.
  • The Global Administrator field is 16 octets and holds an IPv6 unicast address assigned by one of the Internet registries.
  • The Local Administrator field is 2 octets. The organization that holds the address can encode any information there, with the format and meaning defined by the sub-type.
sections.eli5: Each tag has a part that says how far it may travel, a part that says what kind it is, a long part with the owner's address, and a small part where the owner writes whatever note they like.

sections.title: Registrations at IANA
sections.content:
The document defines a new BGP attribute, the IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community, with value 25. IANA created a registry for the class, with future assignments made by the First Come First Served policy of RFC 5226. Transitive types fall in 0x0000-0x00ff and non-transitive types in 0x4000-0x40ff.

Two types are assigned: IPv6 address specific Route Target as 0x0002 and IPv6 address specific Route Origin as 0x0003.
sections.eli5: A central office keeps the list of tag types, and anyone who asks first can get a new type number. Two kinds are already written in.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document adds no new security issues, and all the security considerations for BGP Extended Communities apply. It points to ongoing efforts to improve BGP security and notes a potentially serious issue when a malformed optional transitive attribute is received, which another work in progress at the time discusses.
sections.eli5: The bigger tag is no riskier than the old one, but a badly made tag that gets passed along can cause trouble.

fields.name: Sub-Type
fields.desc: Same sub-types as the IPv4 Address Specific community.

fields.name: Global Administrator
fields.desc: An IPv6 unicast address assigned by an Internet registry.

fields.name: Local Administrator
fields.desc: Any information the address holder chooses; meaning set by the sub-type.
